fills.notes: The preserved tail “...5 a]ll of them” most naturally yields “and all of them”, a common connective in this register, introducing a collective statement.

The clause needs a predication about the totality (“all of them …”) before the purpose/result (“that they shall …”). In the oldest cosmological substrate, bodies/powers are ‘set/established in their places’ according to measure and order.
After “that they shall …” the expected correspondential function is manifestation: the ordered totality exists so as to ‘reveal/show’ what is within (light, measure, order).
“seven people” is almost certainly a Coptic/Greek calque for ‘seven powers/ones’ (heptad as powers), not literal persons. The substrate speaks of powers and measures rather than ecclesial persons.
The word is already mostly given as “per[son ... ]”; completing to “person,” is the minimal restoration.

“the time when [ ... ] of the light” calls for the cosmogonic act proper to this layer: a separation/distinguishing of Light from mixture, prior to any moralizing. Hence “comes the separation of the light”.

fills.fill: is in the heights, and fills
fills.notes: The sequence “of the light [ ... 19 ... ] the universe” requires a relation between Light and the cosmos: Light above, filling/ordering the universe as its inner form. This matches correspondential inside→outside logic (light as form of understanding).

Before “is revealed” the text needs the subject of revelation. In this substrate the “order” (taxis/measure) of the universe is what becomes manifest when the Light is distinguished and seen in effects.
After “is revealed” an appositive extension is expected: order and measures (limits/number/weight) as the revealed structure. This is characteristic of Iranian-cosmological ‘measure’ language.

The surviving “... utt]erly” strongly constrains to “utterly”; what precedes should complete an adverbial pair: ‘wholly/with purity’ fits the substrate’s emphasis on unmixed Light (purity) rather than moral exhortation.
After “the way that he exists …” the natural completion is a statement of mode/essence: existence ‘in his own form’ (i.e., according to his proper degree), aligning with discrete degrees.

“from [ ... ] these other three [ ... ]” points to a contrast between ‘the one’ (single nature/degree) and ‘the other three’ (the triad of degrees or threefold powers). Thus “from the one, and not … these other three …”.
The phrase “these other three …” most coherently closes as “natures” in the oldest layer, marking discrete kinds/levels rather than offices or persons.

assessment: Most gaps can be restored only to the level of structural sense: order/measure, separation of Light, the heptad as powers, and the contrast of one nature with ‘other three’ natures/degrees. Exact wording remains uncertain in several places because the surviving anchors are few (especially #2, #7–#9, #10–#13), but the correspondential constraints (Light as inner form; revelation as manifest order; powers and measures rather than ‘people’) narrow the restorations to a limited semantic range.
